methodologyNotes: Covers standalone consumer satellite messenger / communicator devices used off-grid for two-way or one-way text, location tracking, and SOS. Excludes smartphones with built-in satellite features, fixed marine SSB/VSAT terminals, satellite phones, and emergency-only Personal Locator Beacons (PLBs) that carry no non-emergency messaging. Price is typical US retail for the device only (excludes the required airtime subscription) in USD. network = the satellite constellation the device transmits over (enum: Iridium, Globalstar, Inmarsat, EchoStar). twoWayMessaging = true if the device can both send and receive free-form text messages; false if it is send-only or preset-message-only. standaloneDisplay = true if the device has a built-in screen to read and compose messages without a paired smartphone. physicalKeyboard = true if the device has an on-device keyboard for typing messages. weatherForecast = true if the service can deliver on-demand weather forecasts to the device. batteryLifeHrs = manufacturer-rated battery life in hours at a 10-minute tracking interval; null if not disclosed. batteryType = enum (rechargeable-lithium for built-in USB-rechargeable cells; replaceable for user-swappable AA/AAA batteries). waterproofRating = IEC 60529 ingress protection rating as published (e.g., IPX7, IP67, IP68). weightGrams = device weight in grams including its internal battery. dimensionsMm = length x width x depth in millimeters. null where a manufacturer does not publish a value.

products.name: Garmin inReach Messenger Plus
products.priceNote: US MSRP $500 per the Backpacking Light review, which states verbatim "an MSRP of $500" and lists "msrp $500" in its comparison table. Price is for the device only and excludes the required satellite subscription.
products.provenance: Garmin's official inReach Messenger Plus owner's-manual specifications page (source) confirmed the exact model and gave verbatim the battery type ("Rechargeable, built-in lithium-ion battery" -> rechargeable-lithium) and the water rating ("IEC 60529 IPX7"). The Backpacking Light review (corroboration) identified the same "Garmin inReach Messenger Plus" and stated the price verbatim as "an MSRP of $500" (and "msrp $500" in its spec-comparison table), the weight as "4.1 ounces (116 g)", and the "Iridium satellite network", alongside two-way photo/voice/text messaging and a standalone monochrome display. I also cross-checked Amazon (model "inReach Messenger Plus", IPX7, 1.08" screen, 25-day 10-min tracking) and a BikeTiresDirect page reproducing Garmin's spec sheet (on-demand weather forecasts, MIP screen usable without a phone, 600 h at a 10-min interval) to verify identity and the display/weather booleans; batteryLifeHrs and dimensionsMm are left null because no cited page states them in the methodology's units (hours / millimeters) verbatim.

GPS Trailmasters, an authorized Garmin dealer, lists the base inReach Mini 3 (MPN 010-03387-00, UPC 753759361396) at $449.99 with published specs of "4.31 oz (122.2 g)", "up to 350 hours ... in 10-minute tracking mode", IP67, and the "Iridium satellite network" — all matching the Amazon "Visit the Garmin Store" listing (Model Year 2025, same MPN/UPC, base "No Photo and Voice Messaging" style, which also states weather reports/forecasts and two-way texting). Model identity confirmed as the Motorola Defy Satellite Link (independent Nomadic Supply listing shows MPN "DEFY", UPC 810296025492), not a sibling such as the Defy 2 smartphone; network left null because the service spans multiple GEO constellations ("Inmarsat, EchoStar, and others"), which does not map to a single enum value, and batteryLifeHrs left null because only a "4 days standby" figure is published, not a rated life at a 10-minute tracking interval.

products.name: Somewear Global Hotspot
products.priceNote: Typical US retail MSRP, device only (excludes the required Iridium airtime subscription). Pack & Trail review (May 2024): "The Global Hotspot is usually $349.99 USD but is $299.99 for the holidays." Corroborated by The Prepared (June 2020): "MSRP is $350" and "MSRP: $349". (Andrew Skurka's 2021 review lists "$280 retail"; a 2023 reader comment on that review cites $500; the device later shifted to enterprise/contact-sales.) Reported $349.99 as the standard MSRP.
products.provenance: The Somewear Labs manufacturer product page (somewearlabs.com/product/hotspot) confirms the exact model — the Global Hotspot — a screenless, smartphone-paired satellite device on Iridium's low-earth-orbit network with Micro-USB charging that floats and sends/receives 1000+ messages per charge; it publishes no retail price (B2B "Contact us"). The Pack & Trail hands-on review (May 2024) corroborates the identical model (Global Hotspot, Iridium network, two-way texting via the paired app, 4 oz, Micro USB, floats, IPX7, on-demand weather reports, "10 days battery life with 10 minute tracking") and states the device price "is usually $349.99 USD" — an MSRP independently confirmed by The Prepared (2020: "MSRP is $350" / "MSRP: $349"), while Andrew Skurka's 2021 review gives the weight verbatim as "4.0 oz (113 grams)" and confirms it "lacks a display or other physical buttons." Model identity is certain (same 4 oz Iridium puck, Micro-USB, floats); one discrepancy is noted — the current manufacturer page lists IP68 whereas two independent reviews state IPX7, so the better-corroborated consumer rating IPX7 is reported, and batteryLifeHrs=240 is the exact hours conversion of the "10 days at 10-minute interval" figure stated by both Pack & Trail and The Prepared.
